lesson.title: Writing a Letter: Punjabi Letter-Writing Conventions
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: ਅੱਜ ਅਸੀਂ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਚਿੱਠੀ ਲਿਖਣਾ ਸਿੱਖਦੇ ਹਾਂ। (Today we learn to write a letter in Punjabi.) Punjabi letters follow their own conventions for greetings and closings — different from an English letter.

A Punjabi letter often opens with ਪਿਆਰੇ (pyaare, 'dear') for someone close, or a more formal greeting for someone you respect deeply. The body of the letter states its ਵਿਸ਼ਾ (visha, 'subject' or purpose) clearly, often within the first sentence. A common respectful closing is ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਸਤਿਕਾਰ ਸਹਿਤ (tuhaada satikaar sahit, roughly 'with your respect'), followed by your name. Practice writing a short letter to a family member using this structure: greeting, clear subject, and a respectful closing.
You've now practiced the real structure of a Punjabi letter — greeting, subject, closing. This is a skill you can use to write to family members near or far.

objectives: Use appropriate Punjabi letter-writing conventions: a greeting, a clearly stated subject, and a respectful closing
Write a short, complete letter in Punjabi (or a Punjabi/English mix, if still building fluency) to a family member
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce the three parts of a Punjabi letter: greeting, subject, closing.
2. Practice the key vocabulary aloud: pyaare, visha, tuhaada satikaar sahit.
3. Model a short example letter together, pointing out each of the three parts.
4. Move to the worksheet: write a letter to a family member using all three parts.
5. Read the letter back together, checking that each part is present and clear.
6. Close by discussing: who would the child like to actually send a letter like this to?
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide sentence starters for each part (greeting, subject, closing) rather than a fully blank letter
Ready for more: challenge the child to write the entire letter in Gurmukhi script rather than English transliteration
For a child who enjoys writing, encourage them to actually send the letter to the family member they wrote to
teacherGuide.answerKey: Open-ended writing — check that the letter includes a clear greeting, a clearly stated subject/purpose within the first sentence or two, and a respectful closing before the child's name.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Formal letter-writing conventions are the Grade 7 Punjabi course's core grammar-mastery and cultural-literacy skill, connecting language mechanics to a real, usable family-communication skill.

generationData.instructions: Write a short letter to a family member. Include a greeting, a clear subject, and a respectful closing.
